Dear Dr Cross,

DOB: 20/11/1970
Dear Dr Cross,

I am writing to refer Mr. Collister, a factory foreman who has symptoms and signs suggestive of diabetes
mellitus type 2, for assessment and management.

Mr. Collister is married with 3 children, who has a history of infectious mononucleosis in 2003. However,
he has no known allergies. His recent medical history includes an episode of tonsillitis and sore left
shoulder which were cured successfully.

Initially, he came to my practice in March 2014, complaining of high temperature, sore throat and
productive cough which was settled by rest and salt water gargles. 2 months later, he was prescribed
amoxicillin for tonsillitis. On subsequent visits, he had pain in his left shoulder for which he was referred to
a physiotherapist. Later, he presented with an intermittent right knee pain. As a result, he was advised to
reduce his weight and commence regular exercises.

On 4/1/2015, Mr. Collister has reported feeling tired and dizzy for the last 4 weeks. Furthermore, he is
unfit and overweight. Consequently, blood tests were requested. On review today, his blood tests revealed
an increase in random and fasting glucose levels as well as elevated cholesterol level.
